data.name: Heading
data.comment: The heading of the Output panel: the settings of the video file the export writes (resolution, format, quality). A noun. Keep it to about 14 characters: it is also a tab in a narrow window, beside Timing and Frame.

data.name: ResolutionLabel
data.comment: The label over the list of video sizes (720p to 4K).

data.name: FormatLabel
data.comment: The label over the list of file formats and codecs ("MP4 · H.264").

data.name: QualityLabel
data.comment: The label over the list of quality levels (Standard, High, Maximum): how much detail the video keeps, which sets its file size.

data.name: Checking
data.value: Checking what this PC can encode…
data.comment: Shown in place of the lists until the start-up check has found which video encoders this PC has.

data.name: Ready
data.comment: Read by a screen reader when the lists appear in place of Checking.

data.name: ConservativeNote
data.value: 10Lapse couldn't check this PC's video encoders, so it offers H.264 up to 1080p.
data.comment: The note under the lists when the start-up check of the encoders failed or timed out.

data.name: FormatReplaced
data.value: {0} can't be exported on this PC, so {1} is selected.
data.comment: A notice: a format was replaced because this PC cannot export it. {0} the format chosen before ("HEVC"), {1} the one selected now ("H.264").

data.name: ResolutionReplaced
data.value: {0} can't be exported on this PC with these settings, so {1} is selected.
data.comment: A notice: a resolution was replaced because this PC cannot export it with the project's settings. {0} the one chosen before ("4K"), {1} the one selected now ("1440p").

data.name: ResolutionReplacedByShape
data.value: {0} isn't available for this shape on this PC, so {1} is selected. Your {0} choice comes back with a shape that allows it.
data.comment: A notice: a resolution was replaced because this PC cannot export it in the frame shape chosen now; the choice returns with another shape. {0} the one chosen ("4K"), {1} the one selected now.

data.name: KeepSelected
data.comment: The button under a replacement notice that keeps the selected settings in place of the earlier choice. Keep it to about 24 characters.

data.name: EstimateAbout
data.comment: The Output panel's estimate of the video's file size. {0} the size ("180 MB").

data.name: Megabytes
data.comment: A file size in megabytes: the estimate, the finished file, the photos to download from OneDrive. {0} the number, already written with your decimal separator ("4.2", "173"). Use your language's symbol for megabytes.

data.name: Gigabytes
data.comment: A file size in gigabytes. {0} the number, already written with your decimal separator ("1.8"). Use your language's symbol for gigabytes.

data.name: UnderOneMegabyte
data.comment: A file size under one megabyte, shown alone (the estimate, the finished file), so it starts with a capital letter.

data.name: ResolutionOptionFormat
data.comment: An item of the Resolution list. {0} its name ("1080p"), {1} the width, {2} the height, in pixels ("1920", "1080", written without grouping).

data.name: FormatOptionFormat
data.comment: An item of the Format list. {0} the codec ("H.264", "HEVC"). MP4 is the file type's name; keep it.

data.name: QualityStandard
data.comment: The lowest quality level in the Quality list (the smallest file). An adjective agreeing with your word for "quality" (QualityLabel), as a list item. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: QualityHigh
data.comment: The default quality level in the Quality list; also the last part of the export panel's Output row ("4K · H.264 · High"). An adjective agreeing with your word for "quality". Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: QualityMaximum
data.comment: The highest quality level in the Quality list (the largest file). An adjective agreeing with your word for "quality". Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: GifFormatOption
data.comment: An item of the Format list, after the MP4 items: an animated GIF, a short looping picture for chat and the web. Also the file type in the Save dialog. GIF is the file type's name; keep it.

data.name: GifSizeLabel
data.comment: The label over the list of GIF sizes (Small, Medium, Large), shown in place of Resolution while Animated GIF is chosen. A noun. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: GifRateLabel
data.comment: The label over the list of GIF frame rates (Up to 10 fps, ...), shown in place of Quality while Animated GIF is chosen. Keep it to about 18 characters.

data.name: GifSizeSmall
data.comment: The smallest GIF size (320 pixels on the long side), as a list item followed by its pixel size. An adjective agreeing with your word for size (GifSizeLabel). Keep it to about 10 characters.

data.name: GifSizeMedium
data.comment: The middle GIF size (480 pixels on the long side, the default). An adjective agreeing with your word for size. Keep it to about 10 characters.

data.name: GifSizeLarge
data.comment: The largest GIF size (640 pixels on the long side). An adjective agreeing with your word for size. Keep it to about 10 characters.

data.name: GifRateOptionFormat
data.comment: An item of the GIF frame rate list: the most frames per second the GIF plays (a slower video keeps its own speed). {0} the rate with its unit ("10 fps").

data.name: GifKeepsVideoSpeed
data.value: The GIF keeps your video's speed: {0}.
data.comment: The note under the GIF lists when the video plays slower than the chosen GIF frame rate, so the GIF plays at the video's speed. {0} the video's speed ("8 fps", or "2 s per photo").

data.name: EstimateRange
data.comment: The Output panel's estimate of a GIF's file size, as a range: GIF files vary a lot with the photos (a clear sky is small, foliage is large). {0} the low end ("3.1 MB"), {1} the high end ("6.2 MB").

data.name: EstimateUpTo
data.comment: The Output panel's estimate of a GIF's file size when its low end is under a megabyte. {0} the high end ("1.4 MB").

data.name: PixelSizeFormat
data.comment: A picture's size in pixels, as the export panel and the finished state show a GIF's size ("480 × 270"). {0} the width, {1} the height, written without grouping.
